paper_title: Token-Level Uncertainty Estimation for Large Language Model Reasoning
caption: Left: Uncertainty estimation with different perturbation strength _q. Right: Influence of perturbation strength on uncertainty-based AUROC scores.
model_annotation: The line plot illustrates the relationship between perturbation strength, denoted as σ_q on the x-axis, and a corresponding uncertainty metric on the y-axis, for three different uncertainty estimation methods: AU (red line with circle markers), TU (blue line with circle markers), and EU (green line with circle markers). The x-axis spans perturbation strengths from 0.02 to 0.5 on a linear scale, with labeled ticks at 0.02, 0.05, 0.1, 0.15, 0.2, and 0.5. The y-axis, representing the uncertainty value, ranges from 0.000 to 0.200, with major gridlines and tick labels at intervals of 0.025. The AU line begins near 0.125 at σ_q = 0.02, remains nearly flat until σ_q = 0.2, then rises to approximately 0.158 at σ_q = 0.5. The TU line starts at 0.125, stays relatively constant until σ_q = 0.2, then increases sharply to about 0.192 at σ_q = 0.5. The EU line remains close to 0.000 until σ_q = 0.2, after which it rises steadily to approximately 0.050 at σ_q = 0.5. All lines are solid with circular markers at each data point.
